issues.description: default_raise and orphan comments reference '< 3.10 compatibility' that no longer applies
issues.detail: In chia/wallet/wallet_request_types.py the function default_raise still carries the docstring 'This should be impossible to hit and is just for < 3.10 compatibility', and the comment block above TransactionEndpointRequest still says 'this is for < 3.10 compatibility'. Now that 3.9 is dropped and kw_only is used directly, this rationale is wrong/misleading. Either delete default_raise (and migrate the now-unnecessary field(default_factory=default_raise) sentinels to plain required kw-only fields), or update the comments to explain why the sentinel is still kept.

issues.description: Ruff UP007/UP035/UP045 globally ignored — defers the work the PR description says is the point
issues.detail: The PR description says 'Union types will soon not be supported through Ruff. Use A | B or A | None for Optional[A].' The ruff.toml change instead adds UP045, UP007, UP035 to the ignore list with a TODO. This contradicts the stated intent and creates a latent task that is easy to forget. At minimum, file a tracking issue or convert the TODO into a typed `# noqa` per-file ignore so the project doesn't silently lose the ability to lint new Optional[]/Union[] usage forever.

issues.description: Install script still rejects Python 3.7/3.8 via a stale minor-version check
issues.detail: install.sh now prints 'Chia requires Python version >= 3.10 and < 3.13.0' but the predicate immediately above it is `[ "$PYTHON_MINOR_VER" -lt "7" ]`. That accepts 3.7/3.8/3.9 even though support has been dropped, contradicting the message and the rest of the PR. The bound should be `-lt "10"` to match the new minimum.

issues.description: test-install-scripts.yml leaves debugging `dnf search` calls in CI
issues.detail: The Amazon Linux and Rocky steps now run `dnf update -y` followed by `dnf search python3.12` and then install. The `dnf search` call is purely informational, slows CI, and produces noisy output; it looks like a leftover from debugging. Remove it, and consider dropping the unconditional `dnf update -y` (which can churn many MB on every run) unless it is needed to find python3.12.

issues.description: conditions.py: stale comment about 3.9 coverage quirk left in code
issues.detail: The removed `# pragma: no cover` had a comment 'Something about python 3.9 makes this be not covered but on 3.10+ it is covered'. The pragma was correctly removed, but verify the surrounding `# noqa`/comment cleanup is complete; here it is, but a quick grep for other 'python 3.9'/'< 3.10' comments across the repo would be worthwhile in this same PR to avoid leaving misleading guidance.

issues.description: poetry.lock marker churn: `python_version == "3.10"` for tomli/exceptiongroup/async-timeout will need another bump when 3.13 is added
issues.detail: Markers like `markers = "python_version == \"3.10\""` for tomli, exceptiongroup, and async-timeout are technically correct today (project supports 3.10/3.11/3.12, and the stdlib has these on 3.11+), but pinning to equality instead of `< "3.11"` will silently exclude 3.13 once added. Using `< "3.11"` is more forward-compatible and matches what poetry typically generates. Worth a follow-up.

issues.description: cmd_classes.py: `default=kwargs.get("default", MISSING)` is fine but consider explicit handling
issues.detail: Previously, the code branched on Python version to pick MISSING vs None as the default-default. Now it always passes MISSING. This is correct under kw_only dataclasses, but if a caller passes `default=None` explicitly, the behavior is preserved; if they omit it, MISSING means the field is required. Worth a brief test confirming both code paths still produce the expected click option behavior (required vs default-None).

issues.description: wallet_request_types.py: removed `dataclass_transform` decorator means IDEs/type-checkers may no longer infer kw_only behavior in some setups
issues.detail: Previously, `kw_only_dataclass` carried `@dataclass_transform(frozen_default=True, kw_only_default=True)` so static analyzers knew the resulting class accepted only keyword args. With the helper inlined as `@dataclass(frozen=True, kw_only=True)`, mypy/pyright should still understand it natively, but verify CI's type-check job covers these classes — particularly any constructors called with positional args would now correctly error, which is the desired behavior, but worth a quick mypy run before landing.

issues.description: Inconsistent dnf installation pattern between Amazon Linux and Rocky vs prior `python39`
issues.detail: Rocky previously installed `python39` explicitly, while Amazon Linux did not (it relied on the default). Now both install `python3.12` directly. Confirm that Amazon Linux 2 vs Amazon Linux 2023 both ship `python3.12` in their default repos — on AL2 this may require enabling amazon-linux-extras or EPEL, in which case CI will silently fail when AL2 is selected. If only AL2023 is targeted, document that.

dissents.topic: How aggressively to remove < 3.10 compatibility scaffolding

positions.position: This PR is already large; leave default_raise and the 'for < 3.10 compatibility' comments for a follow-up cleanup PR. The behavior is correct; only the rationale comments are stale.

Dead-code rationale is worse than dead code: it actively misleads future readers. The whole point of dropping 3.9 is to delete the conditionals, including the sentinel functions whose only purpose was working around 3.9's lack of kw_only. Do it now, in the same PR, while the context is fresh.

dissents.topic: Whether to ignore UP007/UP035/UP045 in ruff

positions.position: Auto-converting Optional[X] and Union[A,B] across an entire codebase is high-churn and risks runtime breakage with libraries that introspect annotations. Defer it; the TODO is honest about the deferral.

The PR description claims this conversion is part of the intent. Ignoring the rules globally means no new code can be lint-caught either. At minimum, run `ruff --fix` for these three rules in this PR (it's mechanical), or land them rule-by-rule with separate PRs and remove the ignore.

With kw_only dataclasses on all supported versions, a required keyword-only field can simply be declared without a default. The `default_raise` factory is now pure noise and should be removed; required fields should look required.

There may be Streamable / from_json_dict round-tripping that depends on the field having a default_factory to support partial construction. Removing it could break serialization. Keep it but rename and re-document to reflect the new rationale (not '< 3.10 compatibility').

review.summary: The PR mechanically drops Python 3.9 across CI matrices, installers, pyproject, lockfile, and inlines the kw_only dataclass workarounds (`kw_only_dataclass`, version-gated `option`/`chia_command`/`command_helper`). The mechanics are right and the dataclass simplification is a real win. Three things should be fixed before merge: (1) install.sh still has `PYTHON_MINOR_VER -lt 7`, contradicting the new ">= 3.10" message and allowing 3.7-3.9 through; (2) the CI install-scripts workflow contains debugging `dnf search python3.12` calls that should not be in production CI; (3) the ruff UP007/UP035/UP045 ignore directly contradicts the PR description's stated goal and should at minimum get a tracking issue or be applied in this PR. Stale "< 3.10 compatibility" comments and the now-redundant `default_raise` sentinel in wallet_request_types.py are good follow-ups; reviewers disagree on whether to do that cleanup here vs separately.
